items.title: Declaration of Pecuniary Interest Under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Mohammad Keshvanu and Sunil Bhardwaj, Angus Valley Montessori Kitchener
notes: M. Keshvanu provided a delegation on behalf of Angus Valley Montessori in Kitchener. He provided a brief overview of his organization's operations in Kitchener. He expressed concern about the funding gap Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care and that the demand for childcare in the Region of Waterloo far exceeds the allocated number of funded spaces. He requested that Regional Council leverage unused allocated spaces to be used for childcare spaces and further requested that Council advocate with the province to prioritize this urgent community need.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CSD-CHS-25-003, Increasing Child Care Space Through Modular Child Care
notes:
Barb Cardow, Director of Children`s Services, introduced the presentation related to increasing Child Care Space through Modular Child Care and briefly explained that the Staff recommendation was based on direction from Council to determine an appropriate and affordable option in order to grow a licensed childcare system that meets community needs. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. Amber Robertson, Social Planning Associate, provided a presentation community need for increasing non-profit and affordable childcare spaces. She emphasized the urgent need for these spaces as 8,7000 are currently waiting, however, not-for-profit childcare operators are struggling to find affordable and appropriate sites. Staff determined that existing school properties already meet several important requirements for childcare spaces such as accessibility and green space. In collaboration with the Waterloo Region District School Board (WRDSB), Staff identified various WRDSB sites that are in priority neighbourhoods that would allow for the installation of modular buildings for minimal cost and all ongoing costs would be covered by the childcare operators. Staff is recommending that the Committee support the creation of high 
quality childcare by purchasing two modular 88 space childcare centres.

In response to the Committee, A. Robertson confirmed that the modular childcare spaces are accessible buildings including for individuals using mobility devices. Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Services, further confirmed that the project would not result in an increase to the levy as the not-for profit childcare operator must agree to reimburse the Region with interest. He also noted that the requested funding for this project must be allocated and communicated to the Ministry of Health before the end of October, so the project cannot wait for the 2026 budget, or the funding will be recalled by the Ministry. P. Sweeney clarified that given the community need for affordable childcare spaces, Staff determined that it was appropriate to provide support to the not-for-profit operators through longer lease agreements and lower interest rates, although it is outside of the Region's typical role as a service system manager.

motions.item_title: CSD-CHS-25-003, Increasing Child Care Space Through Modular Child Care
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action as set out in report CSD-CHS-25-003 dated August 12, 2025: a)That the Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer be authorized to issue up to $4.4M of debentures to invest in purchasing up to two 88 space modular child care centres to be repaid with a nominal return on investment through a long-term affordable lease rate with not-for-profit child care operators. b)That the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services be authorized to enter into affordable lease agreements with not-for-profit child care operators identified through an application process supported by Procurement, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor; and c)That the Commissioner of Community Services be authorized to execute a lease agreement with Waterloo Region District School Board to prepare the land for modular child care, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action as set out in report CSD-CHS-25-003 dated August 12, 2025:

a)That the Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer be authorized to issue up to $4.4M of debentures to invest in purchasing up to two 88 space modular child care centres to be repaid with a nominal return on investment through a long-term affordable lease rate with not-for-profit child care operators.

b)That the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services be authorized to enter into affordable lease agreements with not-for-profit child care operators identified through an application process supported by Procurement, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor; and

c)That the Commissioner of Community Services be authorized to execute a lease agreement with Waterloo Region District School Board to prepare the land for modular child care, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.

motions.text: That the meeting adjourn at 4:11 p.m.
